mainTopic: סמיכה and offerings on יום טוב, the Sunday 'day of slaughter' after שבועות, and the seven make-up days of שבועות
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רב אשי shows that the ban on סמיכה on יום טוב does not prove that leaning on an animal's sides is forbidden, because the place where סמיכה is done counts as the animal's back. Then a new משנה begins. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about which offerings may be brought on יום טוב and whether one may lean on them. They also argue about whether the 'day of slaughter' moves to Sunday when שבועות falls on Friday, and they agree that it does when שבועות falls on שבת. On that Sunday the כהן גדול wore regular clothes and people could eulogize and fast, so that no one would think those who say שבועות is always after שבת were right. The גמרא then learns from a פסוק that שבועות has seven days of תשלומין, like פסח. It asks why we don't compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days, and it settles on seven using the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת. Next it explains that the mention of סוכות in the פסוק teaches that סוכות, like פסח, requires לינה. The amud ends by asking where we learn that פסח itself requires לינה.

steps.title: רב אשי: what is near the back counts as the back
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof that leaning on an animal's sides is forbidden. Even if leaning on an animal's sides is allowed on יום טוב, סמיכה is done near the back, and that area counts as the back itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say that leaning on an animal's sides is allowed, anything next to its back is treated like its back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects a proof from the previous discussion. He shows that סמיכה still counts as using the animal, even if leaning on its sides is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion tried to prove from the ban on סמיכה that leaning on the sides is forbidden. רב אשי says this is no proof. The place where we do סמיכה (the head, between the horns) is close to the back, and close to the back is treated as the back. So the ban on סמיכה tells us nothing about the sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like, is the same as

steps.whatToRemember: The area where סמיכה is done is treated like the animal's back, not like its sides.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say that the sides are permitted,
phrases.notes: He means leaning on the animal's sides, which the earlier discussion asked about.

phrases.english: anything that is next to its back is considered like its back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof, from before this section, that leaning on the sides is forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Even granting the challenger's assumption, the case is different because of where on the animal it happens
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If leaning on the sides is allowed, סמיכה should also be allowed and proves nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: סמיכה is done near the back, which counts as the back, so it is still a problem

steps.title: משנה: which offerings on יום טוב, and leaning on them
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow bringing שלמים on יום טוב, without סמיכה, and do not allow עולות. בית הלל allow both, with סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: One may bring peace-offerings on יום טוב but may not lean on them, and one may not bring burnt-offerings. בית הלל say: One may bring both peace-offerings and burnt-offerings, and one leans on them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל about sacrifices on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions here. The first is which kinds of offerings may be brought on יום טוב: בית שמאי allow only שלמים, and בית הלל allow עולות too. The second is whether one may do סמיכה on them: בית שמאי say no, and בית הלל say yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offerings, which are completely burned on the מזבח
Leaning one's hands with weight on the animal before slaughtering it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two questions. One is about which offerings may be brought, and the other is about whether you may lean on them.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
One may bring peace-offerings,
but one does not lean on them,
but not burnt-offerings.
And Beit Hillel say:
One may bring peace-offerings and burnt-offerings,
and one leans on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only שלמים, and no סמיכה. בית הלל: both שלמים and עולות, with סמיכה.

steps.title: שבועות on Friday: is the day of slaughter moved to Sunday?
steps.stepSummary: If שבועות falls on Friday, בית שמאי say the holiday offerings are slaughtered on Sunday. בית הלל say they are not pushed off to after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If שבועות falls on Friday, בית שמאי say: the day of slaughter is after שבת. בית הלל say: there is no day of slaughter after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. This one is about the timing of the holiday offerings when שבועות falls on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the first argument. בית שמאי do not allow עולות on יום טוב. The day after is שבת, when they also cannot be brought, so the offerings wait until Sunday. בית הלל allow them on יום טוב itself, so nothing needs to move to after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the משנה uses for שבועות
The day of slaughter, when the holiday offerings are brought

phrases.english: Shavuot that falls on Friday,
Beit Shammai say:
The day of slaughter is after Shabbat.
And Beit Hillel say:
There is no day of slaughter after Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the first argument to a calendar case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the offerings move to Sunday. בית הלל: they are brought on the holiday, with no Sunday slaughter day.

steps.title: Both agree: if שבועות is on שבת, slaughter is on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: When שבועות itself falls on שבת, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that the offerings are brought on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if שבועות falls on שבת, the day of slaughter is after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us a case where both sides agree. If שבועות falls on שבת, everyone holds the offerings are brought on Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even בית הלל, who allow these offerings on יום טוב, cannot bring them on שבת. So when the holiday is on שבת, the offerings must wait until Sunday according to everyone.

phrases.english: And they agree that if it fell on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This means בית הלל agree with בית שמאי.

phrases.english: that the day of slaughter is after Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a case where the argument from the previous step does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When שבועות falls on שבת, everyone agrees the offerings are brought on Sunday.

steps.title: No festive clothes on that Sunday, so as not to support the wrong view
steps.stepSummary: On that Sunday of slaughter, the כהן גדול does not wear his special garments, and eulogies and fasting are allowed. This shows the day is not שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול does not dress in his garments, and people are allowed to eulogize and fast, so as not to support those who say: שבועות is after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how that Sunday was treated. It was made clear that the day is not a holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since offerings were being brought on Sunday, people might think that Sunday was really שבועות. That is exactly what a group who disagreed with the חכמים claimed. So the כהן גדול wore regular clothes and mourning practices were allowed, to show it is an ordinary day.

keyTerms.meaning: So as not to support or strengthen

steps.whatToRemember: The Sunday of slaughter is a regular weekday. It was treated plainly on purpose, so no one would think שבועות always falls on Sunday.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חכמים shaped how a day was observed in public in order to push back against a wrong view about the calendar.

phrases.english: The High Priest does not dress in his garments,
phrases.notes: This is about the Sunday of slaughter after שבת.

phrases.english: and they are permitted to eulogize and to fast,
so as not to uphold the words of those who say:
phrases.notes: This is the group who disagreed with the חכמים and held that שבועות always falls on Sunday.

phrases.english: Shavuot is after Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the Sunday of slaughter from the previous steps was treated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the Sunday of slaughter, no festive garments are worn and eulogy and fasting are allowed, so the day is not mistaken for שבועות.

steps.title: שבועות gets seven make-up days, like פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא learns from a פסוק that the offerings of שבועות can be made up for seven days, just like פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: How do we know that עצרת (שבועות) has make-up days for all seven days? Because the פסוק says, "On the festival of matzos, and on the festival of שבועות, and on the festival of סוכות." The פסוק puts שבועות right next to פסח to compare them. Just as on פסח the offering can be made up during all seven days, on שבועות it can also be made up for seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a source: a פסוק that lists the holidays side by side. This shows that שבועות, even though it is only one day, has seven days to make up its offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבועות is a one-day holiday, so you might think its offerings must be brought on that day or not at all. רבי אושעיא uses a comparison from the פסוק: because שבועות sits in the same list as פסח, it gets the same seven-day window. This explains the משנה's case, where the offerings of שבועות are brought on Sunday, after the holiday is over.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the משנה and גמרא use for the holiday of שבועות
Make-up days: extra days when you can still bring an offering you missed
Compares one thing to another because the פסוק places them together (a היקש)
The festival of matzos, meaning פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the משנה's ruling that the offerings of שבועות can be brought after the holiday, such as on Sunday when שבועות falls on שבת.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין לָעֲצֶרֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין, כָּל שִׁבְעָה —
phrases.english: From where do we know that Atzeret has make-up days for all seven days?
phrases.notes: עצרת is just another name for שבועות.

phrases.english: As it says: "On the festival of matzos,
and on the festival of Shavuot, and on the festival of Sukkot."
The verse compares the festival of Shavuot to the festival of matzos:

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַג הַמַּצּוֹת יֵשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כָּל שִׁבְעָה —
phrases.english: Just as the festival of matzos has make-up days for all seven days,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת יֵשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כָּל שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: so too the festival of Shavuot has make-up days for all seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: מִנַּיִין לָעֲצֶרֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's assumption that the offerings of שבועות can be brought on a later day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of a היקש to פסח, the offerings of שבועות have seven days of תשלומין.

steps.title: Why not compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we compare שבועות to פסח and not to סוכות, which has eight days of make-up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe you should say the פסוק compares שבועות to סוכות. Just as סוכות has make-up days for all eight days, שבועות should also have make-up days for all eight days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison. The same פסוק also mentions סוכות, so why not compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists all three holidays, so it is not clear which one שבועות should copy. The challenge assumes סוכות has eight make-up days, counting שמיני עצרת. If that is right, choosing פסח and seven days looks arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: "But maybe say...": the גמרא suggests a different possibility
Eight: the seven days of סוכות plus שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: But perhaps say: the verse compares it to the festival of Sukkot,

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת יֵשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כָּל שְׁמוֹנָה —
phrases.english: so just as the festival of Sukkot has make-up days for all eight days,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת יֵשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כָּל שְׁמוֹנָה!
phrases.english: so too the festival of Shavuot should have make-up days for all eight days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of פסח as the model in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of שבועות to פסח that gives seven days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק also lists סוכות, which has eight make-up days, so שבועות could just as well get eight.

steps.title: שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday, so סוכות really has only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eighth day (שמיני עצרת) is a holiday of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eighth day is not really part of סוכות. So סוכות also has seven days, and the number seven stays the same either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמיני עצרת is a separate רגל, then סוכות itself is only seven days. Comparing שבועות to סוכות then gives seven make-up days too, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighth day, meaning שמיני עצרת
A holiday of its own, not part of the holiday before it

phrases.english: The eighth day is a festival in its own right.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: סוכות is only seven days, because the eighth day stands alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סוכות has eight days, so comparing שבועות to it would give eight make-up days.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday, so סוכות also gives only seven.

steps.title: For make-up days, שמיני עצרת does count with סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: שמיני עצרת is separate only for certain laws. For make-up offerings it counts as part of סוכות, as a משנה shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say we call the eighth day a holiday of its own, but that is only for the six differences remembered by the code פז"ר קש"ב. When it comes to make-up days, the eighth day is a make-up day for the first day of סוכות. As we learned in a משנה: Someone who did not bring his holiday offering on the first day of סוכות can bring it during the whole holiday, including the last day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last answer. It shows from a משנה that for make-up offerings, the eighth day does count together with סוכות, so the question of eight days comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday only for specific laws, which are summed up in the code פז"ר קש"ב. For תשלומין, though, the משנה says a person can make up the first day's offering even on the last day (שמיני עצרת). So סוכות really does have eight make-up days, and the challenge of step 7 is back in force.

keyTerms.meaning: "Granted that we said...": accepting a point but limiting how far it goes
"These words apply only...": limits a rule to certain cases
A memory code for six ways שמיני עצרת is different from סוכות
"As we learned in a משנה": brings support from a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not saying that שמיני עצרת is part of סוכות in every way. It is still a holiday of its own for the laws of פז"ר קש"ב. It only counts together with סוכות for make-up offerings.

phrases.english: Granted that we say
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, turning "they say" into "we say."

phrases.english: that the eighth day is a festival in its own right,
that applies only to the matters of PaZeR KeSheV.
phrases.notes: A memory code for six laws where שמיני עצרת differs from סוכות. The גמרא doesn't list them here.

phrases.english: But regarding make-up days,
it is a make-up day for the first day.
As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג —
phrases.english: One who did not bring the festival offering on the first day of the festival

phrases.aramaic: חוֹגֵג אֶת כָּל הָרֶגֶל, וְיוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן.
phrases.english: may bring it throughout the whole festival, and on the last festival day.
phrases.notes: "The last festival day" here means שמיני עצרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמְרִינַן שְׁמִינִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן פָּזֵ״ר קֶשֶׁ״ב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 8 and brings back the question of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its separateness is limited to פז"ר קש"ב. For תשלומין, a משנה shows the eighth day counts together with סוכות, so סוכות has eight make-up days.

steps.title: When unsure, take the smaller number
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a rule: if you grab too much you may end up with nothing, but if you grab a little you keep it. So we choose seven, which is included in eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you did not grab. If you grabbed a little, you did grab.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer with a general rule of reasoning. When there are two possible comparisons, we choose the smaller one, so שבועות gets seven make-up days, not eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסח (seven) and סוכות (eight) are possible models, and the פסוק does not tell us which to pick. Seven is included in eight, so choosing seven is certainly correct for those days. Choosing eight could add a day that has no real basis.

keyTerms.meaning: You grabbed or took hold of

steps.whatToRemember: שבועות has seven days of תשלומין. It is compared to פסח rather than סוכות because of the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: when unsure, we take the smaller amount, which is included in the larger one.
steps.whyThisMatters: תפשת מרובה לא תפשת is a general rule of reasoning that the גמרא uses in many places when a comparison could point to more or less.

phrases.english: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp;
if you grasped a little, you grasped.
phrases.notes: In this case, seven is the "little" and eight is the "lot," so we choose seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּפַשְׂתָּ מְרוּבֶּה לֹא תָּפַשְׂתָּ, תָּפַשְׂתָּ מוּעָט תָּפַשְׂתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that came back in step 9, and confirms step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule for deciding between two possible comparisons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבועות might be compared to סוכות and get eight make-up days.
steps.terutzMaskana: We take the smaller, certain amount: seven days, like פסח.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שבועות has seven days of תשלומין, based on the rule of תפשת מועט.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק mention סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: If שבועות is compared only to פסח, the mention of סוכות in the פסוק seems to have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if we don't compare שבועות to סוכות, what law did the תורה mean to teach by writing 'the festival of סוכות' here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק lists סוכות at all, since we just decided not to learn שבועות from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 chose to compare שבועות only to פסח. That leaves the word סוכות in the same פסוק with no job. The גמרא assumes every word in the תורה must teach something, so it demands to know what this mention teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is this teaching us?

phrases.english: But, for what law
did the Merciful One write the festival of Sukkot?
phrases.notes: The פסוק is דברים 16:16, which lists פסח, שבועות and סוכות together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 10: having set aside סוכות as a source for שבועות, the גמרא asks what the word סוכות in the פסוק teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of סוכות in the פסוק, which now seems to teach nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If סוכות is not the model for שבועות, its mention in the פסוק looks extra.

steps.title: סוכות is compared to פסח for staying overnight
steps.stepSummary: The mention of סוכות teaches a הקש to פסח: just as פסח requires לינה, so does סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written to compare it to פסח: just as פסח requires staying overnight, so too סוכות requires staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word סוכות is in the פסוק to compare סוכות to פסח for one law: staying the night in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mention of סוכות now has its own job. The פסוק puts סוכות next to פסח so we learn a law from one to the other (a הקש). Just as one who brings offerings on פסח must stay overnight in ירושלים, the same applies on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare (to make a הֶקֵּשׁ, learning one thing from another because the תורה places them together)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same פסוק can be used for more than one comparison. שבועות is learned from פסח for the make-up days, while סוכות is learned from פסח for לינה.

phrases.english: To compare it to the festival of matzos:
Just as the festival of matzos requires staying overnight —
phrases.notes: This means staying the night in ירושלים before heading home.

phrases.english: so too the festival of Sukkot requires staying overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by giving the mention of סוכות its own teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra-looking word a different job: a הקש of סוכות to פסח for לינה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of סוכות seemed pointless once שבועות was compared only to פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: סוכות is mentioned in order to compare it to פסח, teaching that סוכות also requires לינה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that פסח requires staying overnight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that פסח itself requires לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, for פסח, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that פסח requires staying overnight. This is a setup line; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 learned סוכות from פסח. That only works if פסח already has a clear source for לינה. So the גמרא now asks for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "There" means פסח: where does the תורה teach that פסח requires staying overnight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 12: since סוכות is learned from פסח, the גמרא now needs the source for לינה on פסח itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that פסח requires לינה
